_readme: The anonrouter-verify command's contract, loaded identically by the JS and Python
suites. Two commands with the same name that disagreed about their exit codes or
their JSON shape would be worse than having only one, because a script written
against either would silently mean something different under the other.
What is pinned here:
exitCodes     0 met, 1 not met, 2 the command itself was wrong. The distinction
between 1 and 2 is load-bearing: a crashed or mistyped command must
never be mistaken for a verification answer.
documentKeys  The exact top-level keys each command prints, in order. Adding one
in a single language is drift.
hopKeys       The keys of a hop object, and the extra keys hop 1 carries.
usageCases    Inputs that must be REFUSED before anything is contacted, with the
phrase the operator has to see. Several of these are security
decisions, not ergonomics: --api-key on argv, and requiring
hardware_verified without an engine to establish it.
neverPrinted  Substrings that must not appear in any document. The evidence body
is ~66 KB of internal compose topology and an API key is a
credential; neither belongs in a CI log.
offlineCase   An origin nothing is pinned for. Both commands must refuse it
without a network call and emit the full document shape, which is
what makes the shape testable with no gateway.

usageCases.name: an unknown option is refused rather than ignored
route needs a provider and a model
an API key on argv is refused by name, not silently ignored
requiring hardware_verified without an engine is refused up front
an unknown assurance state is refused
untrusted is not a threshold anyone may require
a flag missing its value is refused
refusing to fetch collateral without supplying any is refused

offlineCase.name: an origin with no pin fails closed without contacting anything
